seo.title: Help for people without housing in Las Vegas - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help in Las Vegas for people without housing: shelter, meals, showers, health care, benefits, work, documents, safety and pet support.

page.heading: Las Vegas — help for people without housing
page.urgent: Immediate danger, fire or medical emergency: 911 Local services and shelter search: 211 Courtyard Homeless Resource Center: 702-229-6117 Clark County Social Service: 702-455-4270 Mental health or suicide crisis: call or text 988 Domestic violence: call or text SafeNest at 702-646-4981
page.notice: Beds, meals, funds, hours and eligibility can change. Call before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, benefit, medical appointment, treatment, bus pass, housing placement or job on the same day.
page.intro: If you have nowhere safe to stay tonight, start with the Courtyard, an emergency shelter listed below, or Nevada 211. Say where you are, whether you are alone or with family, and whether there is a medical problem, violence, pregnancy, disability, veteran status, a minor or a pet. Coordinated Entry is important for longer-term housing, but it is not required before asking an emergency shelter for help. — tel:+17022296117
page.footer: No Home Help — free, static information without tracking.

entries.title: What to do today
entries.description:
1. Danger, severe illness, overdose or violence happening now: call 911 and give your exact location first.
2. No safe place tonight: call the Courtyard at 702-229-6117, then 211 if you need another option. Ask specifically who can take your household today; a phone call does not reserve a place.
3. Need food, a shower or social services: ask the Courtyard, Salvation Army Day Resource Center or Catholic Charities what is available today. For longer-term housing, request a Coordinated Entry assessment through Clark County Social Service at 702-455-4270.

entries.title: 911 — emergency response
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for immediate danger, serious injury, breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe bleeding, overdose, fire or violence in progress. Give the address, cross streets or a clear landmark before describing what happened.
LVMPD — when to call 911

entries.title: 311 — police non-emergency
entries.description:
Local call: 311; dispatch: 702-828-3111, 24 hours.
For non-emergency police help, a past theft or vandalism, a welfare check or a report when nobody is in immediate danger. Use 911 if a crime, threat or medical emergency is happening now.
Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department contacts

entries.title: Nevada 211
entries.description:
Phone: 211.
Ask for emergency shelter, meals, day centers, cooling stations, domestic violence services, health care, benefits or eviction prevention. The directory helps identify options but does not control capacity or reserve services.
Nevada 211 — housing and shelter directory

entries.title: Courtyard Homeless Resource Center
entries.description:
Phone: 702-229-6117; open 24 hours, seven days a week.
A central starting point for adults experiencing homelessness, with covered sleeping space, restrooms, showers, a day room, pet kennels and connections to partner services. Space and individual services are not guaranteed.
City of Las Vegas — Homeless Services
entries.address: Address: 314 Foremaster Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: Clark County Social Service
entries.description:
Phone: 702-455-4270; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Ask for Coordinated Entry, homeless outreach, rent or utility assistance, transportation help or another county social service. Eligibility, documents, funds and processing time differ by program.
Clark County — CARE and Social Service programs
entries.address: Main office: 1600 Pinto Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89106

entries.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
entries.description:
Call or text: 988, free and confidential, 24 hours.
For suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, mental health crisis or concern about someone else. If there is immediate physical danger or an urgent medical need, call 911.
988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline

entries.title: SafeNest domestic violence hotline
entries.description:
Call or text: 702-646-4981, 24 hours.
Confidential safety planning, advocacy and screening for emergency shelter for survivors and their children. Shelter access begins with a phone interview and depends on capacity. Pets can be accommodated through the program.
SafeNest — emergency shelter

entries.title: Find an active cooling or warming station
entries.description:
Seasonal sites open and close according to current conditions. Call 211 or Clark County at 702-455-4270 for the location operating today. Do not rely on an old flyer or last season’s list.
Ask whether a station allows pets and whether they must be leashed or in a carrier.
Clark County CARE and heat relief

entries.title: Courtyard during extreme weather
entries.description:
The Courtyard is listed as open 24 hours and is commonly included in heat-relief planning. Call 702-229-6117 to confirm the current cooling or warming arrangement, space and pet rules.
Courtyard official information
entries.address: Address: 314 Foremaster Lane

entries.title: Heat illness is a medical emergency
entries.description:
Confusion, collapse, seizure, fainting, very hot skin or inability to drink can indicate severe heat illness. Call 911, move to shade or air conditioning and cool the person with wet cloths while waiting. Do not force liquid into an unconscious or confused person.
Carry water, rest during the hottest hours and refill whenever a staffed site permits it.
National Weather Service — heat safety

entries.title: Make one written plan
entries.description: Write down: where you will sleep tonight, where you can eat, the next appointment, the worker’s name, documents still needed and a backup location. Keep the list with emergency numbers on paper as well as on your phone.

entries.title: At every intake
entries.description:
State urgent facts clearly: child, pregnancy, disability, serious illness, medication, violence, veteran status, trafficking, recent discharge, pet or lack of transport. Ask what is available now, what is not available, the next check-in time and a specific alternative.
Ask for a written receipt, confirmation number or appointment details whenever possible.

entries.title: Protect yourself from theft and exploitation
entries.description:
Do not hand over original documents, phone, benefit card or bank information to a stranger offering work, transport, a room or a shelter place. Meet service providers at the published address and verify their number on the official website.
Tell a trusted person where you are going. If threatened, move to a staffed place and call 911; for non-emergency police response, call 311 or 702-828-3111.

entries.title: Courtyard — 24-hour low-barrier starting point
entries.description:
Phone: 702-229-6117; email: courtyardHRC@lasvegasnevada.gov. — mailto:courtyardHRC@lasvegasnevada.gov
Ask about overnight space, guest services, showers, restrooms, medical care, housing navigation, employment help and pet kennels. The campus is open continuously, but a particular sleeping place or partner service may be full or unavailable.
Official Courtyard information
entries.address: Address: 314 Foremaster Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: MORE street outreach team — City of Las Vegas
entries.description:
Phone: 702-229-MORE (6673).
Request outreach for a person living outside within the city. Give an exact location, description and any known medical or safety risk. The request does not guarantee an immediate response; call 911 for an emergency.
City homeless outreach information

entries.title: Clark County CARE Homeless Outreach Team
entries.description:
Phone: 702-455-4270, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
County outreach connects people outside with assessments, shelter, health, transportation and heat-relief resources. Give a precise location and explain urgent needs; an outreach request is not an emergency dispatch.
Clark County CARE Programs
entries.address: Office: 1600 Pinto Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89106

entries.title: Coordinated Entry — what it does
entries.description:
Coordinated Entry assesses housing needs and prioritizes eligible people for longer-term programs. It does not place everyone immediately and is not required before using an emergency shelter.
Single adults can start through Clark County Social Service at 702-455-4270. Take any identification, disability records, eviction papers, income information and proof of homelessness you have, but ask for an assessment even if documents are missing.
Help Hope Home — Coordinated Entry access points

entries.title: Clark County Coordinated Entry offices
entries.description:
- 1600 Pinto Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89106.
- 3885 South Maryland Parkway, Las Vegas, NV 89119.
- 2432 North Martin Luther King Boulevard, Building 2, Suite D, North Las Vegas, NV 89032.
- 1291 West Galleria Drive, Suite 170, Henderson, NV 89014.
Phone for all offices: 702-455-4270. Confirm current hours before traveling.
Current regional access list

entries.title: Catholic Charities — Men’s Emergency Night Shelter
entries.description:
Phone: 702-385-2662; check-in starts daily at 2:30 p.m.; shelter period runs to 7:00 a.m.
First-come emergency shelter for adult men who can manage their own daily care and do not require on-site medical care. Beds depend on capacity. Catholic Charities is faith-affiliated, but states that a person does not need to be Catholic to receive help.
Catholic Charities — shelter details
entries.address: Vehicle entrance: 1501 North Las Vegas Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89101 Pedestrian entrance: 1504 North Main Street

entries.title: Salvation Army — Day Resource Center and Emergency Lodge
entries.description:
Phone: 702-701-5347. The Day Resource Center publishes daily hours of 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
Day services include showers, laundry, hydration and case management. The Emergency Lodge offers no-fee shelter until capacity is reached. Call for the current line-up time, eligibility and belongings rules. The Salvation Army is a Christian church and service organization.
Salvation Army Southern Nevada — homeless services
entries.address: Address: 35 West Owens Avenue, Building 3, North Las Vegas, NV 89030

entries.title: Las Vegas Rescue Mission — Shelter of Hope
entries.description:
Phone: 702-382-1766. Intake is published daily at 3:00 p.m. and again at 6:00 p.m. after the community meal.
First-come shelter for single men, single women, parents with children and intact family groups. Published stays are up to 14 nights for single adults and up to 30 days for guests with children. Capacity and admission still must be confirmed. The Rescue Mission is Christian and its recovery programming is faith-based.
Las Vegas Rescue Mission — Shelter of Hope
entries.address: Address: 480 West Bonanza Road, Las Vegas, NV 89106

entries.title: The Shade Tree — women and women with children
entries.description:
24-hour hotline: 855-385-0072; main phone: 702-385-0072.
Accessible emergency shelter for women and women with children facing homelessness, domestic violence or trafficking. Intake availability changes daily. The program publishes stays of up to 90 days, case management and pet accommodation through Noah’s Animal House.
The Shade Tree — get help
entries.address: Intake: 1 West Owens Avenue, North Las Vegas, NV 89030

entries.title: Family Promise of Las Vegas — families with children
entries.description:
Phone: 702-638-8806; email: info@fplv.org. — mailto:info@fplv.org
Shelter and housing support for families with minor children. Call before going because intake, appointments and the location used for services may change. Contact does not guarantee motel placement, financial help or a shelter opening.
Family Promise of Las Vegas · national affiliate listing — https://familypromise.org/what-we-do/affiliates/locations-archive/
entries.address: Published affiliate address: 1410 South Maryland Parkway, Las Vegas, NV 89104

entries.title: S.A.F.E. House — domestic violence shelter
entries.description:
24-hour hotline: 702-564-3227.
Confidential shelter for survivors of domestic or interpersonal violence, including single adults, LGBTQIA2+ people, women and children, and men with children. A phone intake is required and admission depends on capacity. There is no charge for shelter services.
S.A.F.E. House — emergency shelter

entries.title: Nevada Partnership for Homeless Youth — emergency youth help
entries.description:
24-hour crisis and Safe Place hotline: 1-866-U-ARE-SAFE (827-3723); office: 702-383-1332.
Young people can request emergency shelter, a Safe Place response or help with food, clothes, hygiene, identification, school and work. The Drop-In Center publishes Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. hours. Call for age rules and availability.
NPHY — get help
entries.address: Drop-In Center: 4981 Shirley Street, Las Vegas, NV 89119

entries.title: If a shelter is full
entries.description:
Ask the worker to name a specific alternative, address, intake time and transport route. Explain if there is a child, pregnancy, disability, medical risk, violence, veteran status or a pet. Try 211, the Courtyard and the shelter type that fits your household.
Do not pay a stranger or unofficial intermediary for a promised shelter bed. For immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911.

entries.title: Catholic Charities — daily community meal
entries.description:
Phone: 702-385-2662. A free public meal is published every day from 10:00–11:00 a.m. in the St. Vincent Lied Dining Facility.
Arrive before the serving period and ask staff about the current line. The organization is Catholic but states that receiving help does not require being Catholic.
Catholic Charities — community meal
entries.address: Vehicle entrance: 1501 North Las Vegas Boulevard Pedestrian entrance: 1504 North Main Street

entries.title: Las Vegas Rescue Mission — daily evening meal
entries.description:
Phone: 702-382-1766. The public community meal is published daily from 5:00–6:00 p.m.; the line forms at the west gate.
Food is available while the service is operating and does not guarantee shelter admission afterward. The Rescue Mission is a Christian organization.
Las Vegas Rescue Mission — basic daily services
entries.address: Address: 480 West Bonanza Road, Las Vegas, NV 89106

entries.title: Three Square Food Finder
entries.description:
Food assistance line: 702-765-4030.
The searchable map is updated regularly with food pantries, walk-up distributions, drive-through sites, senior pantries and meal sites. Ask about a site you can reach without a car and confirm its date, identification rules and whether food remains.
Three Square Food Finder

entries.title: Catholic Charities — Hands of Hope pantry
entries.description:
Phone: 702-387-2291.
A grocery pantry with registration requirements. The current food-bank listing shows Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 8:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m., plus the last Saturday of the month, and says it is closed Wednesdays and the last Friday. Confirm before going because the schedule and supplies change.
Current Three Square listing
entries.address: Address: 1501 North Las Vegas Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: The Just One Project — no-cost Community Market
entries.description:
Phone: 702-462-2253; published call hours are 8:30 a.m.–2:00 p.m.
The Just One Project — food appointment
entries.address: Location: 1401 North Decatur Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89108
entries.how_to_access: Appointment-based grocery shopping with produce, pantry items, dairy and protein. The suite number and service hours differ between current listings, so call for the exact entrance and appointment. The mobile Pop Up & Give markets do not require an appointment.

entries.title: The LGBTQ+ Center — food distribution
entries.description:
Phone: 702-733-9800.
The current Three Square listing publishes a food distribution Wednesday, 9:00–11:30 a.m., while supplies last. Call before going; dates, line procedures and inventory can change.
Three Square Food Finder · The Center — https://thecenterlv.org/
entries.address: Address: 401 South Maryland Parkway, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: Salvation Army — ask about today’s meal and pantry
entries.description:
Phone: 702-701-5347.
The Salvation Army publishes a free community meal and a family food pantry among its Southern Nevada services. Ask the Day Resource Center for the current meal time and whether the food pantry requires a separate appointment or location.
Salvation Army — programs that help
entries.address: Homeless services: 35 West Owens Avenue, North Las Vegas, NV 89030

entries.title: If you need food today
entries.description:
For a predictable public meal, first confirm Catholic Charities at 10:00 a.m. or Las Vegas Rescue Mission at 5:00 p.m. For groceries, call Three Square. Arrive early, bring bags and water, and ask whether an ID or Clarity Card is required.
Do not pay anyone to enter a free food line or public-benefit application.

entries.title: Courtyard — showers, restrooms and day room
entries.description:
Phone: 702-229-6117.
The 24-hour campus has showers, restrooms and a day room. Ask about the current queue, hygiene items, clothing, laundry access and belongings rules before leaving anything with staff.
Courtyard services
entries.address: Address: 314 Foremaster Lane

entries.title: Salvation Army Day Resource Center
entries.description:
Phone: 702-701-5347; daily 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. is published.
Showers, laundry, hydration and case management. Confirm arrival time, items needed and whether the service has reached capacity.
Salvation Army homeless services
entries.address: Address: 35 West Owens Avenue, Building 3, North Las Vegas

entries.title: Catholic Charities — hygiene and clothing for shelter guests
entries.description:
The men’s shelter publishes showers, restrooms, toiletries and linens for admitted guests. Its Client Services Office distributes clothing and hygiene items when available. Ask at 702-385-2662 about eligibility and current office times.
Catholic Charities — shelter and client services
entries.address: Address: 1501 North Las Vegas Boulevard

entries.title: Las Vegas Rescue Mission — hygiene items
entries.description:
The Mission publishes hygiene kits on request, including feminine hygiene products and adult diapers when available. Ask staff at the community meal or call 702-382-1766; supplies are not guaranteed.
Basic daily services
entries.address: Address: 480 West Bonanza Road

entries.title: CARE Complex — lockers, mail and transition services
entries.description:
Phone: 702-685-9102.
A Clark County guide lists lockers, mailbox service, hygiene packages, clothing, internet, ID and birth-certificate help. It also says a referral is required from a social worker, shelter, probation officer, church official or another person assisting with transition. Call to confirm that the service and referral route are current.
Clark County homeless-services guide
entries.address: Address: 200 Foremaster Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: Protect documents and medication
entries.description:
Keep identification, medication, money, benefit cards and your phone with you unless a program gives a written storage procedure and receipt. Ask what is prohibited, how long items are kept and what happens if you miss collection time.
Photograph important papers and email the images to an account only you control. Never give a stranger your PIN, verification code or original identity documents for a promised job, room or benefit.

categories.title: Health, mental health and substance use

entries.title: Medical emergency
entries.description: Call 911 for unconsciousness, trouble breathing, chest pain, severe bleeding, seizure, suspected overdose, serious heat illness or another immediate threat to life. Do not wait for a social-service appointment.

entries.title: Las Vegas Health & Wellness Center — Healthcare for the Homeless
entries.description:
Appointments: 800-787-2568.
Primary care, preventive and women’s health, chronic-disease care, case management, outreach, street medicine, immunizations and telemedicine. Nevada Health Centers states that services are offered at no charge to unhoused individuals. Calling first is recommended.
Nevada Health Centers — Healthcare for the Homeless
entries.address: Address: 1450 North Main Street, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: Southern Nevada Health District — main facility
entries.description:
Community Health Center: 702-759-1700; main number: 702-759-1000.
Primary care, behavioral health, family planning, HIV care, sexual health, pharmacy, immunizations and tuberculosis services. Some services require appointments while others accept limited walk-ins. Ask about cost, identification and the last check-in time.
Health District — services and current hours
entries.address: Address: 280 South Decatur Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89107

entries.title: Martin Luther King Family Health
entries.description:
Appointments: 702-383-1961 or 800-787-2568.
Family medicine, pediatrics, behavioral health and pharmacy. Appointments are recommended and walk-ins are accepted. Insurance is accepted and a sliding-fee discount is available based on income and family size.
Nevada Health Centers — MLK clinic
entries.address: Address: 1799 Mount Mariah Drive, Las Vegas, NV 89106

entries.title: Sexual health, HIV, PrEP and PEP
entries.description:
Phone: 702-759-1700.
The Health District provides sexual-health testing and treatment, HIV care and PrEP/PEP services. Same-day volume can fill early. Call for the current fee, appointment or walk-in process, and tell staff promptly if possible HIV exposure was recent.
Sexual Health Clinic
entries.address: Clinic: 280 South Decatur Boulevard

entries.title: Mental health crisis
entries.description:
Call or text: 988, 24 hours.
Ask for crisis counseling and available local response. If someone has a weapon, is unconscious, is seriously injured or presents an immediate danger, call 911 instead or as directed.
988 Lifeline

entries.title: SAMHSA treatment referral
entries.description:
National Helpline: 1-800-662-HELP (4357), 24 hours.
Confidential information and referrals for mental health and substance-use treatment. Use the official locator and call a facility before traveling to confirm services, cost, insurance and admission availability.
FindTreatment.gov

entries.title: CrossRoads of Southern Nevada — medically supported detox
entries.description:
Inpatient: 702-382-7746; outpatient: 725-726-2535.
Detox, residential and outpatient substance-use treatment. Cost depends on insurance and other factors; calling does not guarantee admission or free care. Alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal can be life-threatening—call 911 for seizures, severe confusion or other emergency symptoms.
CrossRoads — detox information

entries.title: West Las Vegas Library
entries.description:
Phone: 702-507-3980.
Computers, Wi-Fi, scanners, copiers, fax, a legal kiosk and an EmployNV Career Hub. Computer sessions generally require a Library District card and PIN. Ask what identification or temporary access is possible and confirm current hours.
West Las Vegas Library
entries.address: Address: 1861 North Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89106

entries.title: The Center — CyberCenter
entries.description:
Phone: 702-733-9800.
The LGBTQ+ Center publishes two free hours of computer and internet use during Center business hours. Ask about availability, printing and whether an appointment is needed.
The Center — CyberCenter
entries.address: Address: 401 South Maryland Parkway

entries.title: RTC bus information
entries.description:
Customer service: 702-228-7433, published daily 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.
Ask for the route, stop, fare and last bus before traveling. A social-service agency may occasionally provide a pass, but it is never automatic; ask your case manager directly.
RTC Southern Nevada — ways to travel

entries.title: RTC reduced fare
entries.description:
Reduced fares are available to listed groups including seniors 60+, people with disabilities, Medicare recipients, veterans, youth and qualifying WIC participants. A reduced-fare ID and supporting documents are required. Homelessness alone is not a reduced-fare category.
RTC — eligibility and application
entries.address: In-person option: Bonneville Transit Center, 101 East Bonneville Avenue, Las Vegas

entries.title: Phone and charging safety
entries.description:
Ask the Courtyard, day center, library or shelter whether charging is allowed. Keep the phone in sight and do not share the unlock code. Write critical numbers on paper in case the battery dies.
Use public Wi-Fi cautiously. Log out of benefits, banking, email and job sites, and do not save passwords on a shared computer.

entries.title: Access Nevada — SNAP, Medicaid and cash assistance
entries.description:
Use Access Nevada to screen for and apply for food assistance, health coverage and cash assistance. A library, shelter case manager or county social worker may help if you lack a device, email address or documents.
An application is not approval. Keep a confirmation number and copies of everything submitted.
Access Nevada

entries.title: SNAP food benefits
entries.description:
Nevada states that households with little or no money should tell Social Services because they may qualify for expedited SNAP within seven business days. This is not guaranteed; an interview and eligibility review are required.
If you have no address, explain your housing situation and ask how notices and the EBT card can be received safely.
Nevada Division of Social Services — SNAP

entries.title: Clark County financial and housing assistance
entries.description:
Phone: 702-455-4270.
County programs include financial assistance, eviction prevention, fixed-income rent assistance, utilities and some transportation support. Funding, eligibility and documents vary. Apply through the official portal or ask an office for help with a paper application.
Clark County — Applications for Assistance

entries.title: Coordinated Entry for longer-term housing
entries.description:
Ask Clark County Social Service, the Courtyard or another listed access point for an assessment. Coordinated Entry prioritizes limited housing resources according to local criteria. It is not a waiting list with a guaranteed time or placement.
Help Hope Home — access points

entries.title: The Just One Project — housing and workforce screening
entries.description:
Phone: 702-462-2253.
The organization screens for housing navigation, homelessness prevention, rapid rehousing, shared housing and workforce services. Submit an inquiry or call; availability depends on program criteria and funding.
The Just One Project — assistance options

entries.title: Social Security and SSI without a permanent address
entries.description:
A person without permanent housing has the same right to apply for Social Security and Supplemental Security Income benefits as someone who is housed. Benefits may use direct deposit, Direct Express or an approved third-party arrangement.
Social Security: 1-800-772-1213. Ask a case manager or Legal Aid for help with records, appeals or safe mail.
SSA — Spotlight on Homelessness

entries.title: Avoid benefit and housing scams
entries.description:
Do not pay for a public-benefit application, Coordinated Entry assessment or supposed priority on a shelter or housing list. Do not share bank login details, one-time codes or EBT PINs.
Ask for the worker’s name, agency, written program rules and a receipt for any legitimate payment.

entries.title: EmployNV Career Hub
entries.description:
Phone: 702-486-0100.
No-cost career coaching, job search, referrals to training and access to the state job database. Call for current hours, walk-in rules and documents. Participation does not guarantee training funds or a job offer.
EmployNV Career Hub — job seekers
entries.address: Las Vegas location: 3405 South Maryland Parkway, Las Vegas, NV 89169

entries.title: West Las Vegas Library — EmployNV and computers
entries.description:
Phone: 702-507-3980.
The library lists an EmployNV Career Hub, computers, Wi-Fi, scanners, copiers and a legal kiosk. Ask what identification is needed for a library card or computer session and whether a career coach is present that day.
West Las Vegas Library
entries.address: Address: 1861 North Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89106

entries.title: Courtyard and shelter employment help
entries.description:
Ask a Courtyard guest-services worker, Salvation Army case manager, Shade Tree workforce worker or Rescue Mission case manager for résumé help, documents, clothing and a realistic employment plan. Services may be limited to current guests or program participants.
Courtyard partner services

entries.title: Job-search safety
entries.description:
Do not pay an employer for an interview, equipment, a background check by gift card or a promise of work. Do not send a Social Security number or bank details before verifying the employer and receiving clear written terms.
Ask about legal name, pay rate, schedule, work location, transport, uniform costs and when wages are paid. A legitimate job application should not require access to your email or benefit account.

entries.title: Start with a case manager
entries.description:
Ask the Courtyard, Clark County Social Service, Catholic Charities or another shelter case manager to list which document to replace first. Request written proof of homelessness and ask whether the program can receive mail for you before using its address.
CARE Complex and Catholic Charities publish help with IDs or Clarity Cards, but current availability and referral rules must be confirmed.

entries.title: Nevada ID fee exemption for people experiencing homelessness
entries.description:
People under 25 who declare homelessness can receive fee exemptions for an original, renewal or duplicate Nevada ID. People 25 or older may receive a one-time exemption for a duplicate license or ID. All other identity and residency requirements still apply.
Apply in person and use the DMV 128 Declaration of Homeless Status. Ask a case manager to help gather the required original documents and a safe mailing address.
Nevada DMV — ID cards and homeless fee exemptions

entries.title: Replacement Social Security card
entries.description:
Social Security: 1-800-772-1213. A replacement card is free, but acceptable identity and status documents are required. Some people can apply online; others need an appointment.
If documents are missing, ask Social Security and a case manager what records from shelters, schools, employers, courts or agencies can help. Do not pay a private intermediary for a replacement card.
SSA — replacement card process

entries.title: Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada
entries.description:
Phone: 702-386-1070.
Civil legal information, screening and limited representation for eligible people, including tenant rights, Social Security, consumer, family and some immigration matters. Contact does not create an attorney-client relationship or guarantee representation. Act quickly when a notice has a deadline.
Legal Aid Center — contact and disclaimer
entries.address: Address: 725 East Charleston Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89104

entries.title: Nevada Legal Services
entries.description:
Phone: 702-386-0404 or 866-432-0404.
Free civil legal services for eligible low-income Nevadans. The current office listing publishes Monday–Thursday 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. and Friday 8:00 a.m.–noon, with a lunch closure Monday–Thursday. Call or complete intake; help depends on eligibility and capacity.
Nevada Legal Services — contact
entries.address: Las Vegas office: 701 East Bridger Avenue, Suite 400, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: Civil Law Self-Help Center — eviction and court forms
entries.description:
Forms and procedural information for eviction, small claims and other civil matters. Staff cannot act as your lawyer. If an eviction notice or court paper has a deadline, take it with you and seek help immediately.
Civil Law Self-Help Center
entries.address: Address: Regional Justice Center, first floor, 200 Lewis Avenue, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: Mail without a permanent address
entries.description:
Before using a shelter, Courtyard, CARE Complex or social-service address, obtain explicit permission and ask how your name must appear, which mail is accepted and how long it is held.
USPS General Delivery may be available at one designated post office, but the postmaster can require suitable ID or restrict service. Confirm the exact office, addressing format and holding period before anyone sends mail.
USPS — General Delivery

entries.title: Danger right now
entries.description: Call 911. If possible, move to a staffed public place and give dispatch your exact location. Do not confront an abuser, trafficker or attacker to recover belongings.

entries.title: SafeNest — domestic violence
entries.description:
Call or text: 702-646-4981, 24 hours.
Confidential hotline, safety planning, counseling, court support and screening for shelter for survivors, children and pets. The shelter location is confidential and admission begins with a phone interview.
SafeNest services

entries.title: S.A.F.E. House
entries.description:
24-hour hotline: 702-564-3227.
Confidential no-cost shelter, meals, laundry, case management and support for people escaping domestic or interpersonal violence. It serves adults and parents of different genders, including LGBTQIA2+ survivors. Capacity is not guaranteed.
S.A.F.E. House shelter

entries.title: Signs of Hope — sexual assault and trafficking
entries.description:
Rape Crisis Hotline: 702-366-1640; Human Trafficking Hotline: 702-936-4004, both 24 hours.
Advocacy, information and next-step support. For a recent sexual assault, the official guidance directs adults seeking a forensic exam to UMC Adult Emergency Department, 1800 West Charleston Boulevard. A police report is not required merely to ask the hotline for support.
Signs of Hope — get help

entries.title: Southern Nevada Family Justice Center
entries.description:
Phone: 702-828-7714.
One location for advocacy, safety planning, protection-order information, immigration help for survivors, victim advocates and detectives. The published hours are Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; call first. Reporting to police is not required simply to ask what services are available.
Signs of Hope — Family Justice Center information

entries.title: Families with children
entries.description:
Contact Family Promise at 702-638-8806, Las Vegas Rescue Mission at 702-382-1766, or The Shade Tree at 855-385-0072 when appropriate. Tell staff the children’s ages, whether both parents need to stay together, and any disability, custody or safety issue.
Do not separate from a child or sign custody papers solely because someone promises a bed. Ask a qualified advocate or lawyer to explain any document first.

categories.title: Youth, veterans, LGBTQ+ people, migrants, seniors and disability

entries.title: NPHY Drop-In Center and Safe Place
entries.description:
Office: 702-383-1332; 24-hour crisis line: 1-866-827-3723.
Food, clothing, hygiene, bus passes, ID help, school and work support, case management and connections to a safe place. A young person can also ask for Safe Place help at any RTC bus, Las Vegas fire station, participating library or Terrible Herbst store.
Nevada Partnership for Homeless Youth
entries.address: Address: 4981 Shirley Street, Las Vegas, NV 89119

entries.title: Shannon West Homeless Youth Center — ages 18–24
entries.description:
HELP of Southern Nevada: 702-369-4357.
Housing and supportive services for people ages 18–24 who are homeless or at risk, including food, case management, education, employment and behavioral-health support. Completing the online questionnaire does not qualify or place anyone in housing; follow the published intake instructions and expect a capacity review.
Shannon West Homeless Youth Center

entries.title: VA Community Resource and Referral Center
entries.description:
Phone: 702-791-9077. VA publishes walk-in service Monday–Friday; current official pages differ slightly between 6:30 or 7:00 a.m. start and 3:00 p.m. closing, so call first.
Coordinated intake for veterans who are homeless or at risk, with housing, health, mental-health, benefits and employment referrals. Bring military and identity documents if available, but ask for help even if they are missing.
VA Southern Nevada — homeless programs
entries.address: Address: 4461 East Charleston Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89104

entries.title: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
entries.description:
Phone: 877-424-3838, 24 hours.
Veterans who are homeless or at risk, as well as family, friends and supporters, can request connection to VA resources. The call does not guarantee an immediate bed or financial payment.
VA homeless veteran care

entries.title: The LGBTQ+ Center of Southern Nevada
entries.description:
Phone: 702-733-9800.
LGBTQ+-affirming peer groups, health and wellness services, free computer use, a lending library, food distributions and some legal clinics. It is not an overnight shelter. Call for current lobby, health-clinic and program hours.
The Center — general services
entries.address: Address: 401 South Maryland Parkway, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: Catholic Charities — immigration legal services
entries.description:
Appointments: 702-383-8387; Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. is published.
Help with eligible immigration applications and proceedings, including permanent residence, employment authorization, citizenship, asylum, TPS and deferred action. Appointment required. Ask about fees, documents and whether the program can handle your particular case.
Catholic Charities — immigration services

entries.title: Catholic Charities — refugees and eligible entrants
entries.description:
Phone: 702-383-8387.
Case management, employment, food, clothing, health and orientation for refugees and other specifically eligible groups such as asylees, certified trafficking survivors, some Cuban entrants and certain visa holders. Eligibility is based on immigration category, not simply lack of housing.
Migration & Refugee Services
entries.address: Address: 1501 North Las Vegas Boulevard

entries.title: Seniors and people with disabilities — Clark County
entries.description:
Social Service: 702-455-4270.
Ask for senior or disability social work, housing, benefits, transportation and homemaker-service information. Explain mobility, medication, communication, caregiver and accessibility needs. Eligibility and program capacity vary.
Clark County Social Service
entries.address: Senior Services: 1600 Pinto Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89106

entries.title: Nevada Aging and Disability Services
entries.description:
Las Vegas regional office: 702-486-3545; statewide: 866-303-6323.
Information and referral for older adults and people with disabilities, including community supports and protective services. It is not an emergency shelter. For suspected elder abuse, ask for the current reporting route; call 911 if danger is immediate.
Nevada Aging and Disability Services Division

entries.title: Tell every shelter about the animal before accepting a referral
entries.description:
The Courtyard has pet kennels, The Shade Tree works with Noah’s Animal House for residents, and SafeNest states that it shelters survivors with children and pets. Rules and space vary. Confirm whether the animal can remain with you, what records are needed and who is responsible for care.
Do not surrender or abandon an animal based only on an unofficial promise of later reunification.

entries.title: The Animal Foundation — Pet Support Hotline
entries.description:
Hotline: 702-955-5932, published daily 9:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.
Help with lost or found pets, rehoming questions, pet food connections, pet-rent resources and low-cost care referrals. Financial or veterinary help depends on the program and eligibility; the shelter is not a full-service veterinary clinic.
The Animal Foundation — contact · pet care assistance — https://animalfoundation.com/what-we-do/pet-care-assistance/
entries.address: Address: 655 North Mojave Road, Las Vegas, NV 89101

entries.title: Animal emergency or cruelty report
entries.description:
City of Las Vegas Animal Protection: 702-229-6444, option 2; Clark County: 702-455-7710.
Use the number for the jurisdiction where the animal is located. In an immediate threat to people, call 911. Ask the Pet Support Hotline before bringing an owned animal to the shelter because intake rules and fees may apply.
The Animal Foundation — jurisdiction contacts

entries.title: Verification and corrections
entries.description:
This page uses government sources and official provider pages. Because daily capacity, funding and hours change, detailed listings tell you when to call before traveling and do not promise service.
Found a closed service, wrong number or additional resource? See how to contribute or submit a correction on GitHub. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
